findings.source_passage: blew curtains in at one end and out the other like pale flags, twisting them up toward the frosted wedding-cake of the ceiling, and then rippled over the wine-coloured rug, making a shadow on it as wind does on the sea
findings.source_locator: paragraph describing the interior of the Buchanan house, before the two women on the couch
findings.why_it_matters: This is one of the most critically cited sentences in the novel — a set piece of Fitzgerald's prose style whose rhythm, imagery ('frosted wedding-cake,' 'shadow on it as wind does on the sea'), and symbolic charge (the illusory, ephemeral world of East Egg) are signature. The draft replaces it with an ellipsis, erasing the passage entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full curtain passage verbatim from 'A breeze blew through the room' through 'making a shadow on it as wind does on the sea.' Do not compress or paraphrase; this sentence is the voice.

findings.source_passage: The Carraways are something of a clan… the actual founder of my line was my grandfather's brother, who came here in fifty-one, sent a substitute to the Civil War… All my aunts and uncles talked it over as if they were choosing a prep school for me, and finally said, 'Why—ye-es,' with very grave, hesitant faces
findings.source_locator: second section, paragraphs on family background and the decision to go East
findings.why_it_matters: The Civil War substitute detail and the aunts-as-prep-school-committee passage are register-defining comic irony that establishes Nick's ironic, self-aware voice and the Midwestern social milieu against which the East is set. Their absence flattens the narrator's voice in the opening exposition.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at minimum the clan/Buccleuch sentence, the Civil War substitute line, and the aunts' 'Why—ye-es' deliberation. These are compact and need not be cut at 1.0× compression.

findings.source_passage: like the egg in the Columbus story, they are both crushed flat at the contact end… the most domesticated body of salt water in the Western hemisphere, the great wet barnyard of Long Island Sound
findings.source_locator: paragraph describing the two Eggs, before 'I lived at West Egg'
findings.why_it_matters: The Columbus egg simile is distinctively Fitzgeraldian and widely noticed by critics as a signal of the novel's concern with the New World myth; 'most domesticated body of salt water in the Western hemisphere' is a characteristic tonal marker. Both are absent from the draft's compressed version.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the Columbus egg simile and the 'most domesticated body of salt water / great wet barnyard' phrase in the geography paragraph; both are short enough to include at 1.0× compression.

findings.source_passage: There was something pathetic in his concentration, as if his complacency, more acute than of old, was not enough to him any more… 'We've got to beat them down,' whispered Daisy, winking ferociously toward the fervent sun
findings.source_locator: Tom's racist speech at dinner, near its close
findings.why_it_matters: Nick's aside about Tom's 'pathetic concentration' is an interpretive keystone — it frames Tom as hollowed-out and anxious, not merely brutish — and Daisy's winking whisper is a characteristic ironic beat. Both are cut, thinning the scene's thematic texture.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'There was something pathetic in his concentration' observation and Daisy's 'We've got to beat them down' whisper; they are brief and essential to the scene's ironic register.

findings.source_passage: surprising me by opening up again in a flower-like way. 'We heard it from three people, so it must be true.'… The fact that gossip had published the banns was one of the reasons I had come East. You can't stop going with an old friend on account of rumours, and on the other hand I had no intention of being rumoured into marriage
findings.source_locator: closing scene at the Buchanans' door, after Nick starts his motor
findings.why_it_matters: Nick's explanation of why he came East — to escape being 'rumoured into marriage' — is interpretively significant character context that establishes his flight from the Midwest as socially motivated; the 'flower-like' reopening of Daisy is also a characteristic voice moment. The draft collapses this to 'a few last words—nothing to alter the sense,' losing both the content and the voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the engagement exchange including Daisy's 'flower-like' reopening, her 'three people' insistence, and Nick's internal gloss on why gossip drove him East. This is compact (three short paragraphs) and should not be cut at 1.0× compression.

summary: The draft has one high-severity signature loss (the famous curtain/wedding-cake/wind-on-the-sea passage, replaced by an ellipsis) and four medium-severity failures including erasure of the Columbus egg simile, the clan/Civil War-substitute voice passage, Tom's 'pathetic concentration' aside with Daisy's winking 'beat them down,' and the interpretively significant engagement-gossip closing scene — together representing substantial voice and content loss in a chapter at 1.0× compression where no such cuts are warranted.
